title: Stable release selector and endpoint quickstart notes
content:
Goal:
Create an approachable, low-friction UI pattern that lets engineers pick a model variant for an endpoint while making the stability/upgrade contract explicit. The selector should support: stable (pinned), rolling (auto-upgrade), and opt-in canary variants. It must surface latency/cost tradeoffs, show last-tested commit, and make rollback trivial.

Audience:
- Individual engineers and small product teams who want fast endpoint setup
- Platform teams that need guaranteed behavior and auditability for production endpoints

High-level UX ideas (wireframe notes):
1) Quickstart card (first-screen)
   - Title: "Create endpoint — select a model"
   - Left column: model catalog search and filters (family, size, quantization, region). Each result shows small badges: "verified perf", "recommended for chat", and cost indicator (low/medium/high).
   - Right column: preview panel for selected model with three big action tiles:
       a) "Stable (pin exact version)" — short blurb: "Guarantees the model version for this endpoint. Good for production and compliance." CTA: "Pin version"
       b) "Rolling (auto-upgrade)" — blurb: "Receive minor improvements automatically; we keep major changes gated." CTA: "Use rolling"
       c) "Canary" — blurb: "Route a percentage of traffic to this variant for evaluation." CTA: "Create canary"
   - Microcopy note: underneath each tile, show two small lines: "typical latency: 120ms" and "relative token cost: 1.0x" (values pulled from model profile).

2) Version detail flyout (when pin button clicked)
   - Header: model name + version hash + published date + link to model release notes (opens in new tab).
   - Copy variants to test:
       Option A (explicit legal tone): "Pinning this version prevents automatic upgrades. Use when you need repeatable outputs or audited model behavior."
       Option B (developer-friendly): "Lock this endpoint to the current model. Changes only happen if you update it here."
       Option C (concise): "Lock model version (recommended for prod)."
   - UX element: small checkbox: "Allow security patches only (minor fixes)" — toggles whether we will auto-apply critical security backports while keeping behavior locked. Tooltip explains scope.

3) Canary setup modal
   - Input: percentage slider (0.5% — 50%), duration selector (hours/days), traffic criteria (all, by route, by header).
   - Preview: estimated extra cost and mean latency delta (computed from model cost profile).
   - Copy: "Canaries help validate real-world performance without affecting all users."

4) Endpoint creation summary page (pre-create)
   - Show a small diff-like preview of "what will change": new endpoint name, pinned version or rolling, routing policy, selected compute profile, estimated cost per 1M tokens.
   - Warning banner (if pinned older version): "This version is X months old. Consider bumping if there are known bugfixes." Link to changelog.

Accessibility and keyboard flows:
- Ensure tiles are tabbable and the percentage slider supports keyboard + arrow adjustments.
- Announce live updates in the preview panel when filters change.
- High-contrast labels for badges.

Backlog grooming notes (candidate stories + rough sizing):
- ENDPT-412: Implement stable/rolling/canary tiles in create-endpoint flow (3 pts)
- ENDPT-413: Add version detail flyout with security-patch checkbox and release note link (2 pts)
- ENDPT-420: Canary traffic routing UI and backend API (5 pts)
- ENDPT-425: Cost estimation line item for endpoint summary (2 pts)
- ENDPT-430: Add audit log entries for pin/unpin actions and UI hooks to view audit (3 pts)

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- User can create endpoint selecting any of the three patterns and the created endpoint respects the selected upgrade policy.
- Pinned endpoints store an immutable reference to model sha and display it in endpoint details.
- Canary routes are configurable and enforceable; metrics pipeline tags canary traffic.
- UI shows latency and cost estimates for selected model variant.

Copy experiments (A/B set to test in staging):
- Microcopy for pinning: test Option A vs B vs C described above. Measure: time-to-create endpoint and support tickets mentioning "why did model change".
- Confirmation CTA labels: "Pin and create" vs "Create endpoint (pinned)" vs "Create endpoint". Track abandonment.
- Canary explanation: short vs long tooltip versions; measure help-clicks and error rates if users accidentally send 100% traffic.

Edge cases and error states to design: 
- User tries to create rolling endpoint but selected model is deprecated -> show disabled tile with tooltip: "Model deprecated for rolling updates. You can pin this exact version or choose an alternate model."
- Model profile missing cost/latency data -> show small "estimate unavailable" badge and a link: "Run perf test" which triggers a lightweight perf job.
- Pin fails due to version metadata missing -> inline error: "Failed to lock version. Try again or contact support (include model id)." Provide copy for support email template.

Telemetry & observability hooks (product/analytics):
- Track selection events: model search > selected_model_id, selected_variant_type (stable|rolling|canary), canary_percentage, time_to_confirm.
- Emit audit events: PIN_CREATED, PIN_REMOVED, ROLLING_SWITCHED with user id and endpoint id.
- Surface in console: quick filter for endpoints with pins older than X months, endpoints with active canaries.

Developer notes (implementation suggestions):
- API: createEndpoint({name, model_ref: {model_id, version_sha, stability: "pinned" | "rolling" | "canary"}, canary_config?, compute_profile}) -> returns endpoint resource with policy object.
- Backend: store policy as separate column (jsonb) to allow future extension; include last_tested_commit reference.
- Rollouts: reuse existing rollout engine for canary traffic percent; tie to tracing tags for easy observability.

Copy appendix: short pieces to use directly in UI
- Stable tile headline: "Stable — lock the version"
- Stable tile subtext: "Repeatable outputs. Use for production or compliance."
- Rolling tile headline: "Rolling — get improvements"
- Rolling tile subtext: "Minor updates applied automatically; major upgrades require approval."
- Canary headline: "Canary — test in prod safely"
- Canary subtext: "Route a slice of traffic to validate changes before full rollout."
- Warning when pinning old version: "This model has not been updated in X months. Confirm pinning or choose a newer variant."

Open questions for PM/Legal/Trust: 
- What constitutes a "security patch" that can be auto-applied to a pinned version? Need legal review for obligations around automatic changes when customers think they are pinned.
- Data retention policy for canary traffic metrics — how long do we keep raw traces?

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- UX: produce 3 mid-fidelity wireframes for the quickstart card + flyout (owner: Marco) due Feb 24.
- Eng: spike on perf-test-on-demand for models with unknown latency (owner: Jordan) due Mar 3.
- PM: confirm legal stance on security-patch auto-apply and produce copy guidelines (owner: Samira) due Feb 28.

Notes from discussion 2025-02-18 (sync with eng + trust):
- Engineering prefers explicit user opt-in for any auto-upgrade beyond semantic patching; legal flagged the need for a clearer consent flow. Recommendation: keep the "Allow security patches only" checkbox unchecked by default and document the scope in a linkable modal.
- Observability: add a tag to traces for canary traffic to make it trivially filterable in the console.

Link to related docs (for design handoff):
- endpoint-policy-spec.md (internal spec)
- rollout-engine-architecture.pdf

End of doc.
